name: Ho Chi Minh Thought
scope: Ho Chi Minh Thought as the defining sources state it: the Communist Party of Vietnam's official system of views on the basic problems of the Vietnamese revolution, from national-democratic to socialist revolution, formed by creatively applying Marxism-Leninism to Vietnam and drawing on national tradition and the era's learning (Giáo trình tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh, ch. 1; Lê Văn Quý, intro). It covers Ho's own texts the Party's course names as its basis (Bản án chế độ thực dân Pháp 1925, Đường Kách mệnh 1927, the 1945 Declaration of Independence, the Testament) and the Party-leadership and party-building teaching of Lê Văn Quý's study. It excludes the Doi Moi market line, Western or dissident readings, and later Party platforms except where the sources present them as Ho Chi Minh Thought.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VI sets out Ho's building of regular, local and militia forces into a modern regular people's army to defend independence.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The 1945 Declaration pledges the whole nation to use all its strength and even sacrifice lives to defend its liberty and independence against the French return.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Ho's 1930 appeal says imperialist contradictions caused the 1914-1918 war and that a new world war will break out as French imperialism prepares to conquer new colonies.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bản án chế độ thực dân Pháp mocks the French claim to be civilising Indochina (a 'strange kind of civilising') and demands an end to colonial rule.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Giáo trình ch. I says Ho took up the Marxist-Leninist theory of class and class struggle, but also quotes his 1924 report that class struggle in Indochina does not run as it does in the West and that patriotism is the main force.

collective-farming.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III quotes Ho's path from land reform through labour-exchange teams to cooperatives and then higher cooperatives, so collective farming is the aim, reached step by step.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ho's 1924 report and his Bản án chế độ thực dân Pháp (1925) condemn colonial rule run to enrich the ruling country through land seizure, forced labour and taxes.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that officials are the people's servants and that if a government harms the people the people have the right to dismiss it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Giáo trình, ch. 5 (p. 274): at the first government session on 3 Sept 1945 Ho called for a democratic constitution through a general election by universal suffrage, to give a state 'hợp hiến do nhân dân bầu ra', with a drafting committee reporting to the elected National Assembly.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ho was a communist who led a Marxist-Leninist party aiming at socialism (Giáo trình ch. III) and in 1956 called on communist parties to defend the purity of Marxism-Leninism against the enemies of communism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that every regime has a dictatorship and that it is the lock guarding the people's democracy against saboteurs, in a state of working-class character; it doesn't state the aim of holding it until classes disappear.

direct-votes.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII says Ho's early constitutional design gave the people a referendum on the constitution and matters of national destiny, a form of direct democracy, though most power is exercised through elected representatives.

dominated-front.rationale: Ho's 1930 appeal describes a revolutionary camp of the oppressed colonial peoples and the exploited working class of the world, led by the Soviet Union, against the camp of international capitalism and imperialism.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 1945 Declaration celebrates that the people overthrew the monarchic regime of many centuries and set up a Democratic Republic, and the 1946 Constitution Art. 1 (Giáo trình ch. VII) places all power in the whole people.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1945 Declaration proclaims that all men are created equal and endowed with the unalienable rights to life, liberty and happiness.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Ho's 1956 article makes the struggle for national reunification, against the schemes of the US and the Saigon administration to perpetuate the division of the country, a task of the Party.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VIII credits Ho with laying the base of a foreign policy built on respect for independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity and on non-interference in each other's internal affairs.

gradual-change.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III quotes Ho that the steps toward socialism must be taken one at a time and warns against voluntarism, though he also held revolution to be necessary.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III quotes Ho that in socialism whoever works more receives more, whoever works less receives less and whoever does not work receives nothing, with distribution by labour as the principle.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III quotes Ho that independence means nothing if the people enjoy no happiness or freedom, and ties independence to socialism that makes people prosperous and fed.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1930 founding appeal commits the Party to confiscate the plantations and property of the imperialists and the Vietnamese reactionary bourgeoisie and distribute them to the poor peasants.

leader-cult.rationale: In 1956 Ho wrote that socialism can never tolerate the personality cult and admitted it had existed to some degree in Vietnam, which limited the initiative of the people.

national-self-determination.rationale: Giáo trình ch. I says Ho took up the principle of national self-determination in 1919 and held that every people has the right to live and be free, and the 1945 Declaration asserts Vietnam's right to be free and independent.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III says Ho found his 'supreme desire' of independence, freedom, food, clothing and schooling achievable only in scientific socialism, so he held socialism and communism to be the basis for society.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VI sets out Ho's call to meet counter-revolutionary violence with revolutionary violence and to fight the invader with every force, which rejects absolute non-killing.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III and ch. VII give the state the task of building a socialist economy and leading the transition, far beyond protecting people from violence.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III presents Ho's socialism as built through a transition period with mixed ownership forms, which rejects a revolution that needs no transitional stage.

one-party-rule.rationale: Giáo trình tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh, ch. 3 (pp. 82-83, on the revolution's principles): it affirms 'vai trò độc quyền lãnh đạo của Đảng của giai cấp công nhân' in the Vietnamese revolution from national liberation to socialism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that the people are masters and that every citizen must truly take part in managing state affairs, though mainly through the state under Party leadership.

party-commands-army.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VI states that Ho built Party organisation in the army on the principle of absolute, direct, all-round Party leadership of the people's armed forces.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: In his 1956 article Ho endorses Lenin's iron inner-Party discipline and says that socialist democracy does not mean a loss of discipline among Marxist-Leninist parties.

party-own-road.rationale: Ho's 1956 article says each party must define its own methods and that national features matter more and more, yet adds that Marxism-Leninism is the common basis and no party's questions are only its own concern.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that the working class has no interests apart from the nation's, and that only national liberation can fully free the working class.

people-in-arms.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VI describes Ho combining guerrilla and militia with a regular, modern people's army, so a professional army is kept rather than replaced by an armed citizenry.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VI says Ho held revolutionary violence necessary to seize and keep power against counter-revolutionary violence, joined to humanitarian conduct toward prisoners; it doesn't cover violence for other goals.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Giáo trình ch. II says Ho's thought inherits and develops the nation's cultural and moral traditions alongside the best of human culture.

property-fundamental.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III lists four forms of ownership for the transition, including a little capitalist property, on the way to a socialist economy based on public ownership, so private property is tolerated rather than held fundamental.

public-ownership.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III says the socialist economy is to rest on public ownership of the means of production, with the state sector leading the national economy during the transition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ho's 1924 report approves Lenin's refusal to divide white from coloured slaves of imperialism, and the 1945 Declaration affirms that all peoples are equal from birth.

recall-officials.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III and ch. VII quote Ho that the people have the right to dismiss deputies of the National Assembly and councils who prove unworthy of their trust.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: Ho's 1946 appeal calls every Vietnamese to rise against the returning colonialists, saying they would sacrifice everything rather than return to slavery, and to sacrifice to the last drop of blood.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Ho's 1956 article calls for the struggle for national reunification and against schemes to perpetuate the division of the country.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Giáo trình ch. III and ch. VI present revolutionary violence of the masses against counter-revolutionary violence as a principle of Ho's thought, used to win and hold power.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Giáo trình ch. IV quotes Ho calling individualism the fierce enemy of socialism, while ch. III says he held that legitimate individual interest of workers should be stimulated under socialism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Giáo trình, ch. on independence and self-reliance: Nguyễn Ái Quốc held that a nation waiting for others' help 'không xứng đáng được độc lập tự do' and the slogan 'tự lực cánh sinh, dựa vào sức mình là chính'; he still sought international support, so the lean is toward own resources, not against aid.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that the state is a people's democratic state resting on the worker-peasant alliance under the leadership of the working class.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that every regime has a dictatorship and asks who dictates over whom, and describes the state as of working-class character, though Ho also called it a state of the whole people.

state-harmful.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII describes a state of the people, by the people, for the people that Ho wanted strengthened, with dictatorship kept as the lock that guards democracy, so abolishing the state is rejected.

unions-good.rationale: Bản án chế độ thực dân Pháp, ch. VII 'Tổ chức công đoàn ở thuộc địa' (minutes of the Red International of Labour Unions, 1923): organising trade unions in the colonies 'có một tầm quan trọng đặc biệt'; the Giáo trình (ch. 2) also records Nguyễn Ái Quốc joining a union as part of his political life.

vanguard-party.rationale: Giáo trình ch. I and ch. IV quote Ho calling the Party the vanguard of the working class, equipped with Marxism-Leninism to lead the revolution.

women-suffrage.rationale: Ho's 1930 appeal pledges equality between man and woman, and Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Art. 1 of the 1946 Constitution, drafted under him, that all power belongs to the whole people regardless of sex, after his call for universal suffrage.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Giáo trình ch. VII quotes Ho that the state rests on the alliance of workers and peasants under working-class leadership.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Giáo trình ch. V and ch. III say Ho counted the national bourgeoisie, which is anti-imperialist and patriotic, among the forces of the great national unity and of building socialism.

workers-own-party.rationale: Giáo trình ch. I and ch. IV quote Ho that the Communist Party of Vietnam is the party of the Vietnamese working class and its vanguard, founded by him.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Ho's 1924 report says the colonial peoples are unremittingly exploited by imperialist capital, which takes their land and leaves them in famine.

summary: Ho Chi Minh Thought is the Communist Party of Vietnam's official ideology, combining Marxism-Leninism with Vietnamese national liberation. It treats independence, national unity and socialism as one project led by the Party, with the peasantry and the working class as its base. It stresses a state of the people, a strong state sector, anti-colonialism and an ethic of frugal, selfless service by cadres.

missingStatements.text: Genuine patriotism cannot be separated from internationalism among working people of all countries.
missingStatements.rationale: Ho states that genuine patriotism can never be separated from proletarian internationalism, and builds the whole doctrine on that link.

missingStatements.text: Public officials should live modestly and serve the people, practicing thrift, integrity and selflessness.
missingStatements.rationale: Cadres are to be leaders and loyal servants of the people and are taught industriousness, thrift, integrity and public-spiritedness.

notes: Searched the Party textbook (Giáo trình), Lê Văn Quý's study, Ho's 1924 report, 1945 Declaration, 1956 article and Bản án chế độ thực dân Pháp for economy, state and democracy, the Party, army and war, colonialism, race and equality, unity and class alliances, ethics and culture, religion, women, minorities, and unions. Most modern issue statements (gender, drugs, environment, technology) have no stated position and stay null; answers that rested on Wikipedia or inference were nulled.
